author: Amanda Mull
description: Downloads of rival AI tool Claude soar amid feud with the Pentagon.
title: ChatGPT Backlash Reveals New Pitfalls in Aligning With Trump

author: Ewa Krukowska, Alberto Nardelli
description: The European Union is set to discuss short-term options to lower energy prices in the coming years, while the green transition takes effect.
title: EU to Consider Options to Cut Energy Prices This Decade

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Swiss lawmakers recommended that voters reject a proposal from right-wing groups to enshrine permanent neutrality in the constitution, a plan that would limit the country’s ability to impose economic sanctions.
title: Swiss Lawmakers Want to Keep Neutrality Flexible Amid Isolationist Push

author: Ellen Milligan, Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer addressed criticism that the UK government has been slow in its response to the conflict in the Middle East, saying “we are and we have done everything we can at speed.”
title: UK Seeks to Quiet Accusations Its Iran Response Was Flat-Footed

author: Omar Tamo
description: Iran is increasingly relying on drones rather than missiles to attack Gulf states as the war in the Middle East drags on.
title: Iran Shifts From Using Missiles to Drones in Gulf Strikes

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, James Attwood, Jack Ryan
description: The Trump administration has struck a deal that would see Venezuela’s state mining company sell as much as 1,000 kilograms of gold to commodities trader Trafigura, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Trafigura Strikes Deal to Buy Venezuela Gold in US Pact

description: The US-Israeli war on Iran entered a sixth day with little sign of easing, as the Islamic Republic vowed to intensify its retaliation and oil extended gains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Vows to Intensify Retaliation While Trump Hails War Gains

author: Fiona MacDonald, Sam Dagher
description: Gulf Arab states have been taking the brunt of Iranian attacks in a war they didn’t start and never chose.
title: Gulf Frustrated at Being the Center of War That’s Not Theirs

author: Amara Omeokwe
description: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Tom Barkin said the central bank’s response to the US-Israel war with Iran will depend on how long the impact on the US economy lasts.
title: Barkin Says Fed Response to War Depends on Length of Shock

author: Annie Lee
description: The US Defense Department is seeking information for the potential stockpiling of five critical minerals, as the country steps up efforts to reduce risks in the supply chain and bolster domestic feedstock.
title: US Defense Department Seeks Information to Expand Metal Stockpiles

author: Piotr Skolimowski, Agnieszka Barteczko
description: Poland’s central bank chief laid out a proposal to generate as much as 48 billion zloty ($13 billion) from the sale of gold reserves to finance defense spending as part of a plan backed by the nation’s president, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Polish Central Bank Chief Weighs Gold Sales to Fund Defense

author: Anthony Halpin
description: A surge in oil prices driven by the US-Israel war on Iran won’t solve the Kremlin’s budget problem, but it could help Russia replenish rapidly depleting rainy-day reserves.
title: Iran War Gives Russia Brief Window to Rebuild Reserves

author: Golnar Motevalli, Patrick Sykes
description: Iran‘s top clerics are nearing a decision on the country’s next supreme leader after Ali Khamenei was killed in the US-Israeli war on the Islamic Republic, with the wartime council laying bare divisions among political factions over the succession and the signal it would send to Tehran’s adversaries.
title: Iran Poised to Name New Supreme Leader With US Watching Closely

author: Alicia A. Caldwell, Paayal Zaveri
description: The Trump administration’s overhaul of the US visa system for highly skilled immigrants is about to get its first major test.
title: Companies Stare Down $100,000 Fee With New H-1B Visa Rules

author: Swati Gupta
description: The US won’t give India the same kind of economic advantages it gave China, which allowed that country to emerge as a major competitor, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau said on Thursday, signaling Washington’s cautiousness in negotiations over a trade deal.
title: US Won’t Allow India to Become Rival Like China, Official Says

author: Godfrey Marawanyika
description: Zimbabwe is taking steps to clear the $23 billion it owes multilateral institutions, as talks with lenders progress well, President Emmerson Mnangagwa said.
title: Zimbabwe Taking Steps to Clear $23 Billion Debt, President Says

author: Samy Adghirni
description: France has reached out to the governments of Italy and Greece to coordinate efforts in the Eastern Mediterranean as tensions over the war in Iran flare, a person close to French President Emmanuel Macron said.
title: France, Italy, Greece to Help Ensure Red Sea Shipping Transit

author: Macarena Munoz Montijano, Michael Nienaber
description: Spain’s top diplomat accused German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of failing to show sufficient backing for a European Union partner when US President Donald Trump threatened to halt trade with the Iberian nation over its opposition to the war on Iran.
title: Spain Scolds Germany’s Merz Over Slight During Talks With Trump

author: Gerry Doyle
description: President Donald Trump’s suggestion that the US would insure and protect oil tankers and other vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz may potentially bring Iran’s anti—ship missiles into play, adding a new dimension to a conflict largely defined by air power.
title: Strait of Hormuz Escorts May Trigger Iran’s Anti-Ship Missiles

author: John Liu, Yujing Liu
description: As US tariffs reorder supply chains and Donald Trump moves from one military campaign to the next, China offered its answer to a more volatile world: staying the course at home.
title: China Makes Stability Top Task in Volatile World Shook by Trump

author: Nectar Gan
description: The world’s second-biggest economy is running out of steam and that has implications for governments the world over.
title: China’s Waning Growth Has Global Repercussions

author: Ani Avetisyan
description: Azerbaijan threatened to hit back after two Iranian drones struck its territory of Nakhchivan, accusing Tehran of escalating regional tensions.
title: Azerbaijan Threatens Response After Iranian Drones Hit Exclave

author: Andrea Jaramillo
description: Las encuestas muestran ahora que quienquiera que suceda a Gustavo Petro tendrá que dar prioridad a limpiar el desastre que dejaron sus reformas fallidas y su costosa disputa con las aseguradoras de salud.
title: Muerte de niño de 7 años desata indignación frente al sistema de salud en Colombia

author: Andrea Jaramillo
description: Polls now show whoever succeeds Gustavo Petro will have to prioritize cleaning up the mess left by his failed reforms and costly feud with medical insurers.
title: A 7-Year-Old Boy’s Death Inflames Anger Over Colombia’s Health Crisis

author: Max Chafkin, Lydia Beyoud
description: So far, Musk’s super PAC money has done little to sway a Kentucky race.
title: Elon Musk Is Backing ‘JD Vance 2.0.’ Some Republicans Aren’t Sure That’s a Good Thing

author: Josh Wingrove, Joe Lovinger
description: President Donald Trump watched from the sidelines for months as three Texas Republicans hammered each other over a US Senate seat, burning through tens of millions of dollars in a vicious campaign that raised Democratic hopes that they could win in November.
title: Trump’s Rapid Shift on Texas Senate Race Underscores GOP Risks

author: Alberto Nardelli, Jorge Valero
description: The European Union is considering providing Ukraine with financial help to repair the Druzhba oil facility as Hungary and Slovakia block support for Kyiv and sanctions on Russia until supplies through the pipeline resume.
title: EU Weighs Aid to Fix Ukraine Oil Plant at Center of Loan Delay

description: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana says that the nation has the ability and resources to withstand the impact of war in the Middle East. Speaking on Bloomberg Television, he also discusses debt consolidation and foreign investment. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: South Africa Can Withstand Mideast Impact, Godongwana Says

author: Bilal Hussain
description: Pakistan is willing to halt operations against Afghanistan if the Taliban government stops supporting militant groups from its territory, the country’s top military leader Field Marshal Asim Munir said.
title: Pakistan Army Chief  Links Peace to Afghanistan Ending Terror

author: Lucy White
description: Another multimillion pound donation from crypto investor Christopher Harborne again propelled Reform UK to the top of Britain’s political fundraising table in the fourth quarter of last year.
title: Farage Outraises Rivals With £3 Million More From Crypto Donor

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, Donald Trump said the US is doing “very well” in its military campaign against Iran, even as the timeline and objectives remain unclear. Iran has vowed to retaliate after the US sunk an Iranian warship off Sri Lanka's coast. 

China set its annual economic growth goal at a range of 4.5% to 5%, the least ambitious expansion target since 1991.

Today's guests: DHL Group CEO Tobias Meyer, Adviser to the Israeli Prime Minister & Aleph Partner, Michael Eisenberg & Raymond James Global Head of Private Capital Advisory Sunaina Sinha Haldea. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Says US Doing ‘Very Well’ & Iran Vows Retaliation | Daybreak Europe 03/05/2026

author: Swati Gupta
description: Narendra Modi’s key ally in Bihar is set to step down as chief minister, a move that could give the prime minister’s ruling party greater scope to consolidate its control in the politically crucial state.
title: India’s Powerful State Leader to Resign, Boosting Modi’s Grip

description: The conflict in the Middle East is causing logistical and financial troubles to the aviation industry. The number of canceled flights to Middle East hubs surpassed 23,000 since fighting began last weekend. Thousands of passengers have been stranded in the Gulf region, forcing many to take circuitous, expensive routes to reach functioning airports in Saudi Arabia and Oman. Bloomberg’s Leen Al-Rashdan breaks down the situation.
title: Canceled Flights to Mideast Top 23,000 Since War Started

description: Damaged building follwoing attacks in Tehran, on March 4. Photographer: Fatemeh Bahrami/Getty Images
title: Israel, Iran Continue Strikes as Middle East Conflict Enters Sixth Day

author: Dan Williams, Christine Burke, Kateryna Kadabashy
description: The US-Israeli war on Iran entered a sixth day with no sign of easing, as the Islamic Republic said its retaliation against American strikes would escalate.
title: Trump Lauds US War Effort as Iran Vows to Escalate Retaliation

author: Olesia Safronova
description: US-brokered peace talks between Kyiv and Moscow initially planned for this week are postponed indefinitely due to the war in Iran, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
title: Ukraine Says Peace Talks With Russia on Hold Due to Iran War

author: Andra Timu, Irina Vilcu
description: The country used to be one of the most dynamic in the region. Now it’s faced with some of the worst metrics in Europe.
title: From Roaring Economy to Recession, Romania Confronts New Reality

author: Andrea Palasciano, Alberto Nardelli
description: NATO plans to push Europe’s debate over security beyond spending increases at its July summit in Turkey to focus on how member states will target investments into technologies that define modern warfare, according to alliance officials.
title: NATO to Shift Focus From Tanks to Drones, AI at July Summit

author: Laura Davison
description: The Trump administration and Venezuela’s state mining company finalized a deal that would see the South American country selling as much as 1,000 kilograms of gold to US markets, the news website Axios reported on Wednesday.
title: Trump Team, Venezuela Broker Gold Export Deal, Axios Reports

author: Katharine Gemmell, Weilun Soon
description: A bulk carrier signaled it was Chinese-owned as it transited the Strait of Hormuz this week, highlighting how vessels are trying to ensure safe passage through the waterway during the war in the Middle East.
title: Bulk Carrier Claiming to Be Chinese Passes Through Hormuz Strait

author: Rong Wei Neo, Weilun Soon
description: Two Russian oil cargoes that had been signaling East Asia as a destination have switched to India, according to ship-tracking data, suggesting New Delhi is becoming more willing to take the crude as the Middle East conflict worsens.
title: Russian Oil Cargoes Swing Back to India as Iran War Hits Supply

author: Nectar Gan
description: Attendance at China’s National People’s Congress in Beijing fell to its lowest level since President Xi Jinping came to power in 2012, highlighting the churn inside the country’s top legislature as a widening purge of officials rolls on.
title: China Top Lawmakers Meeting Is Smallest Ever Under Xi Amid Purge

author: Claire Jiao, Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said the war in the Middle East will test global economic resilience and warned that “new shocks in different shapes and sizes” will keep coming.
title: IMF Says Mideast War to Test World Economy, Expecting New Shocks

author: Shoko Oda, Yusuke Maekawa
description: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. Chief Executive Officer Sultan Al Jaber will meet Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo on Thursday as the war in the Middle East chokes energy flows to Asia.
title: Adnoc Boss and UAE Minister Al Jaber in Japan to Meet Takaichi

author: Stephen Stapczynski
description: A Russian liquefied natural gas tanker sanctioned by the US halted its journey in the Mediterranean Sea after a nearby ship was allegedly attacked by Ukrainian drone boats.
title: Russia LNG Tanker Halts in Mediterranean After Another Attacked

author: Brian Platt, Laura Dhillon Kane
description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said “one can never categorically rule out” participation in military action resulting from the war in Iran, and the country will stand by its allies if necessary.
title: Carney Won’t Rule Out Military Action If Mideast Conflict Widens

description: Canada and Australia are middle powers charting their own course "in a more uncertain, more divided world," Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said during a joint press conference with Australia's Anthony Albanese. (Source: Other)
title: Canada's Carney on Middle Powers, Iran Conflict

author: Heesu Lee
description: The US military said it remained committed to defending South Korea against the nuclear-armed North after local media reported that Washington was considering redeploying regional US military assets to the Middle East as conflict with Iran spirals.
title: US Affirms Korea Defense After Report on Moving Weaponry to Iran

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: President Donald Trump has endorsed US Attorney Kurt Alme to run as the Republican contender for a Montana Senate seat, now that the incumbent, Steve Daines, is not running for reelection.
title: Trump Endorses Alme for Montana Senate as Daines Steps Aside

author: Emily Birnbaum
description: Tech groups representing major companies including Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Apple Inc. are urging President Donald Trump to reconsider designating Anthropic PBC a national security risk, arguing the move would cause detrimental ripple effects for the rest of the industry.
title: Tech Groups Urge Trump to Drop Anthropic Supply-Chain Risk Label

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Dana Stroul, Research Director at The Washington Institute for Near East Policy and former assistant deputy secretary of state for the Middle East under the Biden Administration, weighs in on the next phase of US-Israel strikes on Iran. Representative Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL) discusses why she doesn’t support the War Powers Act and shares her thoughts on the US-Israel strikes on Iran.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: War Powers Resolution Fails Vote in Senate | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/04/2026

author: Jon Herskovitz
description: The US sinking of an Iranian warship off Sri Lanka’s coast has unsettled India’s calibrated response to the war in the Middle East and could strain the government in New Delhi, according to Bloomberg Economics.
title: US Sinking of Iran Ship Piles Pressure on India’s Modi, BE Says

author: Swati Gupta
description: Nepal kicks off its first general election since a Gen Z-led uprising that ousted the former government last year, with a new crop of young candidates emerging to challenge the old guard’s grip on power in the Himalayan nation.
title: Nepal Election Pits Ex-Rapper Against Old Guard Vying for Gen Zs

author: John Liu, Jing Li
description: China’s defense spending will grow by 7% in 2026 — the slowest pace since 2022 — a figure that comes as officials from Washington to Berlin to Tokyo boost their own outlays.
title: China Plans Slowest Boost to Defense Spending Since 2022 at 7%
